emily (Acme): Hey team — around 09:20 UTC our rerank calls started failing. Some requests return 410 MODEL_DEPRECATED, others return 200 but every item has score: 0.0. This hit our production autocomplete. Sample request we send:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-2021-v1", "queries":["how to reset password"], "candidates":["reset password guide","password reset link"]}'

Response (example):
HTTP/1.1 410 Gone
{"error":{"code":"MODEL_DEPRECATED","message":"model redwood/rerank-2021-v1 is retired"}}

And another successful 200 we got moments later: 
[{"id":"reset-password","score":0.0}, {"id":"pw-reset-link","score":0.0}]

Ticket #INC-2247. Can you advise quick mitigation? This is causing incorrect results in search.

jason-support: Thanks @emily — sorry about the disruption. I'm escalating to Eng and SRE. Can you confirm the exact model id you sent in the body and the request-id header from one failed call (X-Request-Id)? Also which tenant/org id?

emily (Acme): model in body is exactly "redwood/rerank-2021-v1". Request id from failed 410: req_0a7c9f2d. Org: acme-corp-42.

priya-eng: looking at logs for req_0a7c9f2d — router rejected because the model id was retired last week. We had an alias that should redirect old ids to the new stable reranker, but the redirect only applies to inference route resolution. If client sets model explicitly in payload (legacy SDKs do), the model lookup bypassed the alias lookup and hit a retired model handler. That returns 410 instead of a graceful alias mapping.

Log excerpt: 
[router] ERROR model_lookup failed 
  model_id="redwood/rerank-2021-v1" 
  code=MODEL_DEPRECATED 
  route=legacy-rerank-pool 
  note="alias-redirect-missed-by-body-override"

priya-eng: I also see separate requests that routed to the fallback pool (legacy shard) where score normalization pipeline was disabled during a maintenance change last month — that explains the 200+zero-score responses. So two issues coincided: (1) retired model id caused 410s, (2) some traffic still hitting legacy pool with normalization off produced zeros.

ryan-sre: we can do a fast mitigation: (A) repoint aliases so the body model lookup uses alias resolution, (B) roll back the normalization pipeline change on legacy pool or drain traffic from the legacy pool. I'm going to purge the routing cache for the retired id now. ETA ~10–15m.

priya-eng: short workaround for customers: change model in request to the replacement id "redwood/rerank-2024-stable" or add query param "?model_alias=rerank-stable" until we finish the routing cache fix. Example: 

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank?model_alias=rerank-stable" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"queries":["how to reset password"], "candidates":["reset password guide","password reset link"]}'

priya-eng: We're also going to add a clearer deprecation header in 410 responses that suggests the replacement id so clients get automated guidance.

deploy-bot: POST /admin/aliases/purge model=redwood/rerank-2021-v1 -> 200 OK (started cache purge across edge clusters).

ryan-sre: cache purge complete in us-west-2, rolling across other regions now. Normalization rollback scheduled to complete in 12 mins.

jason-support: @emily when you have a minute can you try swapping to rerank-2024-stable and confirm if results come back with sensible non-zero scores? Also please include a sample request-id if you still see 410s so we can trace.

emily (Acme): Doing a quick test now... switched to rerank-2024-stable -> returns 200 and scores look reasonable. No 410 on the test. Thanks. :thumbsup:

emily (Acme): A couple follow-ups — why did the alias not redirect in their case? Our SDKs shouldn't be breaking on a model rename like this.

priya-eng: root cause summary: the client's SDK was populating a literal model field in the request body; our server code historically prioritized body.model over alias resolution. During the deprecation we implemented alias redirects for path/route resolution but missed the body override path. That combined with the legacy pool normalization change produced the outage pattern.

Action items we opened: 
- [ENG-452] Patch router so body.model undergoes alias resolution (short-term patch rolled out).
- [SRE-311] Re-enable normalization in legacy pool and add canary tests to validate non-zero scoring (done).
- [DOCS-88] Add clearer deprecation guidance and include replacement model id in 410 responses (in progress).
- [SUPPORT-76] Notify customers with pinned model ids and recommend migration steps.

jason-support: We'll follow up in the ticket and send an advisory for customers pinned to old ids.

emily (Acme): Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please keep me posted once docs/advisory are live.

priya-eng: will do. Marking this thread as resolved once we ship the deprecation header and notify pinned customers. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployment: router-patch v1.3.7 -> success (edges: all regions)

jason-support: Closing the incident in the console and adding the postmortem link to the ticket. If you see anything else, re-open the ticket or ping me here.

emily (Acme): Confirmed everything is green on our side. Thanks again!
